vo: Monday, seven forty-five.
Memory is not in class.
Before the first lesson begins, her mother already knows.
This is Acalink.
One system for everyone in a Malawian school.
Here is everything it does today.
The head teacher sees the whole school.
Attendance, performance, and a class monitor that shows which lessons are really being taught.
At-risk learners come with the reasons, and exam readiness shows who is on course.
Timetables build themselves, or the assistant reads a photo of the one you already have.
Manage students, classes, staff, exams, the calendar, lesson plans and announcements.
Notices can be written in English, Chichewa, or both.
Discipline, health, leave and cover, transport, admissions, boarding and inventory are all here too.
When a boarder signs out, the guardian is told straight away.
Teachers take the register in a few taps, and enter marks on the MANEB scale.
The assistant drafts homework questions, and a lesson plan starts from just a topic.
At term end, the grades work themselves out.
Every report card can carry a written insight for parents.
The bursar sets the fee structure, records payments, and prints receipts.
Arrears, sponsors, bursaries and expenses stay in order, and the head teacher decides who is cleared for exams.
Reminders go out on WhatsApp, and parents can pay by mobile money.
The school always receives the full amount.
Directors compare every campus and approve transfers.
Administrators manage accounts, settings and backups, with an audit log of who changed what.
And the library handles lending, returns and fines.
Run Malawian, Cambridge or Abeka side by side, each with its own grading scale.
Parents get their own app for attendance, results, homework, the calendar, fees and messages.
And alerts arrive on WhatsApp first.
Every module is included in every plan.
Priced per learner, per term, in kwacha.
Register your school at Acalink dot M W.
